entities.summary:
Francisco de Montejo y León was a Spanish conquistador in Mexico and Central America who played a key role in the conquest of the Aztec Empire. Born in 1479 in Salamanca, Spain, Montejo joined Hernán Cortés's expedition to Mexico in 1519 and led the capture of the city of Tenochtitlán in 1521. This victory marked the end of the Aztec Empire and paved the way for Spanish colonization of the region.

The conquest was a result of Montejo's military prowess, strategic alliances with local tribes, and the support of the Catholic Church. The spoils of war included vast amounts of gold, silver, and other precious resources, which fueled further Spanish expansion in the Americas.

Montejo's legacy extends beyond his own time period, as he played a significant role in shaping the course of Mexican history. His descendants continued to hold power and influence in Mexico for centuries, with Montejo himself being granted the title of Marqués de la Piedra by King Charles V in 1525.

A final testament to Montejo's enduring impact is the numerous historical accounts of his life and conquests, which have been documented through various texts, including the works of Spanish historian Bartolomé de las Casas.
